attribution.note: The proposition rests on Marcus's own sentence in his own post. The Veliz summary he quotes is context only and is not the claim being scored.

semantics.note: Faithful past-tense observation. The draft keeps the 'last-minute negotiations' qualifier and does not add any scope Marcus did not state.

contract.note: Marcus set no threshold for 'significantly'. Reading it as material reductions in distinct safeguards is an ordinary, fair plain reading. The contract does not require every provision to have weakened.

evidence.note: This is the bill author's dated summary of the Aug 15 amendments. It confirms criminal perjury penalties were replaced with civil ones, the standard moved from reasonable assurance to reasonable care, and pre-harm enforcement was narrowed. It is an interested party's account, but the contract prefers it.

Independent CalMatters report dated Aug 19, before the post. It corroborates the removal of the Frontier Model Division and of criminal perjury penalties. A cosponsor quoted in it says removing the division weakened the bill.

Same announcement as e1. It qualifies the scale of the change: some of the division's functions moved to the Government Operations Agency, and pre-harm enforcement was narrowed rather than eliminated. These are still reductions, so it qualifies the claim but does not contradict it.

reviews.rationale: The Aug 15 amendments, agreed in negotiations days before Marcus's post, cut several safeguards. They removed criminal penalties, eliminated the new oversight body (moving only some of its functions elsewhere), lowered the attestation standard to reasonable care, and narrowed pre-harm civil penalties. The bill author's summary and independent reporting both record this. These are material reductions, which meets the plain-reading support condition. The qualifications in e3 do not amount to preserved protections.
